title: Defender's cost on test scratch files is measured and settled by the operator
goal: A Defender performance recording of one tests.py run names the processes, paths and extensions that the scans cost, and the operator's choice for the test scratch root (no change, Dev Drive, or a dedicated excluded folder) is applied and timed.

gates.question: May an administrator record Defender's scans during one tests.py run (New-MpPerformanceRecording, then Get-MpPerformanceReport -TopPaths -TopProcesses -TopExtensions)? It changes no setting but needs an elevated PowerShell on the host.
options: yes, the operator runs it and saves the report
yes, an agent runs it in an elevated session the operator opens
gates.recommendation: yes, the operator runs it and saves the report
gates.answer: yes, an agent runs it in an elevated session the operator opens (the Windows host's working session already runs elevated)

gates.question: Where do the test suites' scratch trees live on this host? The per-user Temp folder (pytest's default) is on Microsoft's list of folders never to exclude.
options: no change: keep the default Temp root with synchronous scanning
a Dev Drive (VHDX, at least 50 GB) holding the clone and a test temp root, with Defender performance mode (asynchronous scans; Microsoft's recommended alternative to exclusions)
a dedicated folder outside the profile (for example C:\kb-test-scratch) with a Defender folder exclusion, used only through PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT
a contextual exclusion of that folder limited to ScanTrigger:OnAccess
gates.recommendation: a Dev Drive (VHDX, at least 50 GB) holding the clone and a test temp root, with Defender performance mode (asynchronous scans; Microsoft's recommended alternative to exclusions)
gates.answer: no change: keep the default Temp root with synchronous scanning

notes: Machine changes are the operator's: no agent changes Defender, disks or CPU caps. Each option is timed with the same command before and after, on an idle host, and the result goes in the report. What each option gives up: no change keeps full synchronous scanning at the measured cost; a Dev Drive keeps scanning but defers it until after the open (less protection than synchronous, more than an exclusion), needs 50 GB, admin rights and a second volume, and its trust must be re-applied if moved; a folder exclusion stops scanning of that folder entirely and must never be the per-user Temp folder; a contextual OnAccess exclusion still lets on-demand and behaviour scans run. The CI container is not helped by a host scratch-root change: whether host scanning reaches writes inside the hypervisor-isolated container is an open gap (kb/public/_gaps.md, windows/dev-drive). The scratch-root gate is answered: no change, the default Temp root stays with synchronous scanning, so the story records the cost and applies no machine change. It runs on the Windows host in the same session as ST-pg5jyebo, whose trigger it waits on through depends_on. Housekeeping 2026-10-06: 'perfcheck time tests --max 600' went with the old suite; the bound is now perfcheck time --max-seconds 60, the Windows ceiling of _tools/tests_ceiling.json. Its checks pass before the work on the macOS host by design: they pin that the measurement and the operator's choice lose no test and keep the run within the Windows ceiling, which is what the work must make hold on the Windows host. 2026-10-07: the time bound follows the win32 ceiling raised to 150 s (D-776rvpx2, gate ceiling of ST-pg5jyebo).
